newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Moderate Australian wages data boosts rate cut hopes.
newsitem.headline: Moderate Australian wages data boosts rate cut hopes.

text.p: Australian averages weekly wages grew a lower-than-expected 0.5 percent in the second quarter, figures on Thursday showed, cementing market expectations of another cut in official interest rates as early as Friday.
Figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed that average weekly earnings rose by 0.5 percent in the three months to May for an annual rate of 3.7 percent.
It was the lowest quarterly rise since August 1994 and the annual rate came in well below the 4.5 percent danger zone seen by the Reserve Bank of Australia as a threat to low inflation.
Market forecasts had centred on a 0.8 percent rise for a 4.1 percent annual rate.

Economists said the figures showed that record low inflation announced on Wednesday should be locked in for at least a year. It was more a question of when, not if, the RBA would cut interest rates again to reduce unemployment.
"There doesn't seem to be anything standing in the way of another rate cut," said Michael Blythe, senior economist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
"With an unemployment rate of 8.5 percent it would seem to be a necessity rather than something that I would like to debate," he added.
The RBA has cut the official cash rate four times over the past year, bringing it down to 5.5 percent. But the cuts have so far failed to work through to business and consumer confidence.
